back: The last date known when you make a forecast. Everything after it is hidden from the model.
Expanding trains on all data up to the origin. Sliding trains on the last W points only.
Move the origin forward step by step; at each origin train, forecast the horizon, and compare with the truth.

front: Why add a gap in a backtest?
back: To copy real delays: labels or data that production cannot see at forecast time are hidden.

front: Why report error by horizon step?
back: Error grows with distance. One average hides how far ahead the model is still useful.

front: Which folds count in a backtest?
back: Only complete folds, where the full test horizon exists in the data.
